clue.text: Always contributing to raid as individuals

indicators.note: one piece contributing to another goes into it, so the word for always sits inside the raid

parts.note: a sally is a sudden sortie or raid
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone always joins in a raid, but each acts on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Severally is a formal adverb meaning separately, each one on its own.

clue.text: Sucker with no science subjects upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the pieces upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: the arts are the subjects that are not sciences

explanation.surface: A gullible person upset because science lessons have been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking straw is something you suck through, so a sucker.

clue.text: Vodka, lots drunk, I see consumed here?

indicators.note: consumed means the letters are swallowed inside the jumbled drink
drunk suggests these letters are reeled about and rearranged

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Lots of vodka knocked back, and I see it drunk in this city.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixing VODKA LOTS gives VLADOSTOK, which takes in I and V. The definition is just 'here', made fair by the rest: a Russian port where vodka would be drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladivostok is a Russian Pacific port, a place where vodka is famously consumed.

clue.text: Rung in later, shattered

indicators.note: shattered means broken to pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A bell rung later, sounding shattered.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratline is one of the small ropes across a ship's shrouds that sailors climb like ladder steps.

clue.text: Deficient writing has edge over good stuff

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Weak prose that has an advantage over quality material.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipogram is a text that deliberately omits one letter, so it lacks something by design.

clue.text: Raised concern about a plant

indicators.note: in a down clue raised sends the letters upward, reading them backwards
about means the word for concern goes around the A

parts.note: worry means concern

explanation.surface: Someone voiced unease about a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering herb with feathery leaves, also called milfoil.

clue.text: Vote against party

definitions.meaning: to vote against is to ..., read as ...
a British slang word for a lively party or celebration

explanation.surface: A politician refusing to back the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE A NO, the answer means cast a negative vote; whole, it is British slang for a knees-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is old British slang for a jolly celebration, a party with food and drink.

clue.text: Poster of British lumberjack

parts.note: a logger fells trees, a lumberjack

explanation.surface: A billboard picture of a UK tree-feller.
explanation.definitionFit: A blogger posts entries online, so is one who posts.

clue.text: In hearing, assist a woman

indicators.note: in hearing means the words are taken by their pronunciation, not their spelling

parts.note: aid a, assist a, said as one word

explanation.surface: A hearing aid to help a lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a female first name, so stands for a woman in crosswords.

clue.text: Bonus run in passage of play by means of wide

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
thro is a short form of through, by means of
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: an extra run scored via a wide ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an overthrow is a run scored when a fielder's throw at the stumps goes past them.

clue.text: Return to the stage and do double-take?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to act again, going back to the theatre
a double-take is a delayed startled response

explanation.surface: An actor coming back to the boards and looking twice in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-take is a startled second look, one example of responding to something.

clue.text: VIP swaps penthouse finally for a ministerial residence

indicators.note: swaps signals that one letter of the VIP word is exchanged for another
for names what the closing letter of penthouse is traded for, the A

parts.note: a personage is an important person, a VIP

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of penthouse

explanation.surface: A celebrity trades a luxury penthouse for a vicar's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish priest, a minister of the church.

clue.text: Having work in cafe, give up spot in play

parts.note: waiting at tables is the job of staff in a cafe
to forgo is to give something up
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: A cafe worker sacrifices their spot in a theatrical production.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting for Godot is Samuel Beckett's famous absurdist stage drama.

clue.text: Mild exposure leads to debility entering university: I'm grateful for admission

indicators.note: leads means the leading letters, one from each of the next two words
admission means one piece is let into another

parts.note: a college is a university or part of one
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A weakened man going into college, thankful to be let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' takes the leading letters of both 'debility' and 'entering', which looks like an insertion signal but is not one here.
explanation.definitionFit: A décolletage is a low neckline revealing a little of the chest, a modest bit of skin on show.

clue.text: Couple study a length of part of digestive system

parts.note: a duo is a couple
a den is a study, a private room for work

explanation.surface: A pair examine a stretch of gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Duodenal is the adjective for the duodenum, the first section of the small intestine.

clue.text: Abbey not quite so upright, receiving onset of lightning strike

parts.note: Downton Abbey is a British television period drama

indicators.note: receiving means the letter goes inside
in a down clue upright turns the word upward, reading it backwards
onset of picks the first letter of lightning

explanation.surface: A storm strikes a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: Downton Abbey is a British TV period drama about an aristocratic country house; trimming it gives the first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To down tools is to stop work in protest, to go on strike.

clue.text: Some soldiers not exactly right to return ammunition

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
CA, circa, means about or not exactly

explanation.surface: Troops, not quite on target, sending ammunition back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracer is ammunition that leaves a visible trail when fired, so its path can be seen.

clue.text: Firm sort of wave in middle of kiss

indicators.note: in middle of means one piece sits within another

parts.note: buss is an old word for kiss
a sine wave is a kind of wave

explanation.surface: A firm sort of wave during a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A business is a company, a firm.

clue.text: Matey greeting observer heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for observer is to be taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: a watcher is an observer

explanation.surface: A spectator hears a friendly hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Wotcha is informal British slang for hello, a casual greeting between pals.

clue.text: Sharpen pen, being blunt perhaps

definitions.note: a noun phrase, the state of being blunt, matching the noun answer

parts.note: to hone is to sharpen
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Sharpen a pen, since it is blunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty includes frankness; being blunt is one example of speaking truthfully.

clue.text: Bribe given to a disreputable house

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
low means base or disreputable

explanation.surface: A backhander handed over for a seedy property.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a type of single-storey house.

clue.text: After study put up companion in private Italian course

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the word for private

parts.note: a GI is a private soldier in the US Army

indicators.note: after means the companion follows the reversed study
in a down clue put up sends the letters upward, reading backwards

parts.note: to con is to study
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: After studying, someone set up a friend on a private Italian class.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnocchi are small Italian dumplings served as a pasta course.

clue.text: Accepting pressure, substantially cut prominent article

indicators.note: accepting means one piece takes another inside

parts.note: to slash is to cut heavily

explanation.surface: Under pressure, a newspaper cuts a front-page feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a story given big headline treatment on a newspaper's front page.

clue.text: Having conducted surgery, pipes up about working to finish all off?

op is short for operation, surgery

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around another here

parts.note: risers are vertical pipes carrying water upwards
on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A surgeon, the operation done, plumbing the pipes before finishing the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To take no prisoners is an idiom for acting ruthlessly, killing every enemy rather than capturing them.

clue.text: Wrong American gets a hole in the head

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A misguided American gets a head injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a cavity in the skull bones, literally a hole in the head.

clue.text: Be a fine scout, tricky to confuse

indicators.note: something tricky is intricate and twisted, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Being a good scout, the trick is to bewilder.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make something obscure or unclear, bewildering whoever tries to follow it.

clue.text: Cope shortened to a considerable extent

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to fare is to cope or get on

explanation.surface: A cut-down cleric's cloak goes a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Far as an adverb means by a great deal, as in far better.

clue.text: Country has moved a range of mountains

indicators.note: the A is lifted out of the country's name and put back elsewhere

parts.note: China is a country

explanation.surface: A nation that has shifted a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains is a connected series of peaks, a mountain range.

clue.text: Jet, for example, crossing Peru regularly

indicators.note: one word crossing another goes across it and so surrounds it

parts.note: say means for example

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of Peru

explanation.surface: An aircraft flying over Peru on a schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet of water is a spray, a forceful stream of droplets.

clue.text: Breathy sound of dogs reaching pole, having kept north

indicators.note: having kept means the dogs hold the letter for north inside

parts.note: huskies are sled dogs
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: Sled dogs panting their way to the pole, heading north.
